name: TeacherTool
tagline: A German iPad and Mac app for teachers to track grades, attendance, seating plans and class records offline.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The data model here is not hard: classes, students, assessment types with weights, grades, absences, a computed average. An agent can produce a local-first PWA that does all of that in a weekend, and for one teacher tracking their own courses that is genuinely enough. What it will not produce is the part that matters in a real classroom: a tap-fast interface you trust while thirty people watch, reliable offline behaviour on an iPad, seating plans, and the pile of German school specifics like Bundesland grading keys, oral versus written weighting rules and report-ready exports. Those are years of accumulated edge cases, not a schema. Build it if you want your own spreadsheet with better math, not if you need something that survives a full school year of paperwork.
coreLoopDIY: A local, offline-capable gradebook that stores classes and students, records weighted assessments and absences, and computes per-student averages with a configurable grading scale.
requirements: Node and a browser, ideally an iPad added to home screen as a PWA
A decision about your own grading scale and weighting rules
Your own backup discipline, since all data lives on one device
whatYouLose: Native iPad speed and reliability during a live lesson
Seating plans, photo rosters and the other classroom-specific views
Prebuilt German grading keys, weighting presets and state-specific report logic
Device sync and any backup story you did not write yourself
A decade and a half of teachers finding bugs before you did
moatNotes: Grade data is a whole school year of manual entry, which makes migrating away from anything painful and makes trusting a homemade tool with it a real bet.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because the cost of losing a term of grades is enormous and the cost of the app is a one-time fee. Teachers pay for something that already knows how German assessment works, opens instantly on an iPad, and has been used by thousands of colleagues without eating their data. A DIY build has to earn that trust across ten months of daily use, and there is no shortcut to that.
notes: The math is trivial, the trust is not.
prompt:
Build a local-first gradebook web app for a single teacher. No accounts, no server, no telemetry, no cloud.

Stack, no substitutions:
- Vite + React + TypeScript
- Dexie (IndexedDB) for all storage
- Tailwind for styling
- vite-plugin-pwa so it installs to an iPad home screen and works fully offline

Data model in Dexie:
- Course: id, name, schoolYear, gradingScaleId
- Student: id, courseId, firstName, lastName, note
- AssessmentType: id, courseId, name, weight (number)
- Assessment: id, courseId, typeId, title, date, maxPoints (nullable)
- Grade: id, assessmentId, studentId, value (number), excused (boolean)
- Attendance: id, courseId, studentId, date, status (present | late | absent | excused)
- GradingScale: id, name, entries of { label, min, max } used to map a numeric average to a label

Screens:
1. Courses list, create and edit courses, set assessment types and weights.
2. Course roster: add students individually or paste a newline-separated list of names.
3. Assessment view: pick an assessment, enter grades down the roster with large tap targets, arrow-key and Enter navigation, autosave on every keystroke.
4. Attendance view: pick a date, one tap per student to cycle present, late, absent, excused.
5. Course overview table: one row per student, one column per assessment, a weighted average column, and the mapped scale label. Excused grades are excluded from the average, not counted as zero.

Also required:
- Export all data to a single JSON file and import it back, with a visible warning that this is the only backup.
- Seed one demo course with eight students and two assessment types on first run, clearly labeled demo and deletable.

Out of scope, do not build: multi-user support, sync, sharing, PDF report cards, seating plans, timetable, any AI feature.

Deliver a README with setup commands and one paragraph on how to install it on an iPad.
